report.summary: Chunk 2/7 of graph_delta.py: defines MutationDelta class with detected/detected_leaky properties and SCORING_LAYERS; implements _ast_refs, _literals_by_function, _module_literals (partial).
risks: _ast_refs | low | Multiset flattening uses '#i' suffix; if symbol names contain '#' this could collide. | Check if any function->identifier path contains '#'; unlikely but possible.

_literals_by_function | medium | Constant values are clipped to 80 chars; loss of information may hide changes in long literals. | Verify if any mutation involves literals longer than 80 chars that change only beyond the clip point.

symbols.note: Dataclass with layers, skipped_reason, SCORING_LAYERS constant, detected and detected_leaky properties, to_dict method.

symbols.name: MutationDelta.detected
symbols.note: Property returning True if applied and any SCORING layer moved.

symbols.name: MutationDelta.detected_leaky
symbols.note: Property returning True if applied and any layer moved (including leaky).

claims.text: ``code.refs.leaky`` is deliberately excluded: it scans raw source, so the corpus's own "SEEDED DEFECT" comments move it for every single mutation and a verdict built on it would be a tautology.
claims.why: Chunk does not contain definition or mention of 'code.refs.leaky'; cannot verify exclusion or behavior.

claims.text: Detected means a SCORING layer moved. It does NOT mean the defect was understood — only that the graph is not blind to it.
claims.why: Code returns self.applied and any(l.moved for l in self.layers if l.layer in self.SCORING_LAYERS).

claims.text: What the measurement would claim if comments counted. Reported so the artefact has a number instead of a footnote.
claims.why: Code returns self.applied and any(l.moved for l in self.layers) (all layers, not just SCORING).

claims.text: THE ARTEFACT THIS EXISTS TO REMOVE. The first run of this module reported 10/12 detected, and every single detection contained the tokens ``SEEDED`` and ``DEFECT`` — the marker words the corpus writes into its own replacement comments. ``graph.identifiers`` scans raw source, so comments are tokens, and the measurement was detecting the LABEL rather than the defect. That is the same self-prediction artefact ``eval/ceiling.py`` separates with its clean and leaky arms, and it is why both arms are reported here.
claims.why: References to 'graph.identifiers', 'eval/ceiling.py', and historical run results are outside this chunk.

claims.text: Comments do not exist in an AST, and docstrings are skipped explicitly, so what remains is names the program actually uses.
claims.why: Code parses with ast.parse (ignores comments) and explicitly removes docstring from function body.

claims.text: MULTISET, not a set. Set semantics erase the deletion of a call that still occurs elsewhere in the same function -- and "this function now calls _verify_reachable once instead of twice" is exactly the kind of change a seeded defect makes. Counting is independently correct, not a tune to the answer: it was wrong before the result was known.
claims.why: Code uses Counter to count occurrences, then flattens with '#i' suffix to preserve multiplicity in a set.

claims.text: Three of the five mutations the reference layer missed change no name at all: ``FREE_LANES`` gains ``"claude_cli"``; a host constant gains ``localhost``; an argv list loses ``--no-textconv``. A name-based view is structurally blind to every one of them, because the identifiers are identical before and after.
claims.why: References to 'reference layer' and specific mutations are outside this chunk.

claims.text: Constants are a multiset per function, like references, so losing one of two identical flags is visible. Values are stored as ``repr`` and CLIPPED: this layer must never become a way for a secret in a literal to travel into a report.
claims.why: Code uses Counter per function and clips repr to MAX_REPR (80 chars) with ellipsis.

observations.what: SCORING_LAYERS tuple is a class attribute, not instance; used in detected property.
_ast_refs uses ast.walk on entire tree but only processes FunctionDef and AsyncFunctionDef nodes for body; then walks each statement. This may miss top-level names outside functions.
Multiset flattening uses '#i' suffix; if identifier names contain '#' this could cause collisions. Unlikely but possible.
_literals_by_function also skips docstrings and clips values to 80 chars; loss of information may hide changes in long literals.
_module_literals is incomplete in this chunk; only signature and partial docstring shown.
